title: KV coherence and quant kernel locking rules
body:
Summary:
This document defines invariants, locking rules, and kernel compatibility constraints for the low-precision execution paths (INT8, FP8, GPTQ, AWQ) with special attention to KV cache coherence and scheduler interactions. The goal is a minimal-surface, auditable policy the runtime can enforce at compile-time and runtime to prevent silent correctness regressions and to bound recovery behavior in mixed-precision environments.

Context and design goals:
- Problem: multiple quantized kernel families exist with different memory layouts, alignment, and activation scaling semantics. When combined with distributed KV caches, dynamic model routing, and preemption-friendly scheduling, we must avoid corrupting KV state or producing nondeterministic outputs across fallback transitions.
- Goals:
  - Define per-kernel compatibility markers the scheduler and model-loader can check quickly.
  - Ensure KV cache entries remain readable across safe transitions (read-compatibility) or are invalidated in a deterministic manner.
  - Provide a locking model that minimizes stalls for high-throughput batching while preventing concurrent kernel/model swaps from invalidating in-flight KV access.
  - Define error/fallback semantics (graceful fallback to higher-precision path, kv-invalidation thresholds, metrics to emit).

Assumptions and constraints:
- Models are split into two categories: stateful (uses KV cache across tokens, e.g., decoder-only with caching) and stateless (no KV or KV short-lived). Most safety-critical transitions involve stateful models.
- Kernel families: INT8 (per-channel affine quant), FP8 (E5M2/E4M3 variants), GPTQ (post-training quant with custom layout), AWQ (rowwise asymmetric quant). Each family provides a capability descriptor (binary metadata) published with the model artifact.
- KV cache format: currently a contiguous tensor per layer of shape [batch, head, num_kv, head_dim] with an accompanying metadata header: {model_id, model_version, kernel_cap_id, seq_start, dtype_tag}.
- Scheduler can preempt running batches but will not preempt individual token generation once token dispatch to kernel has started (safety simplification).

Capability descriptor fields (minimal set):
- kernel_cap_id: short stable string (e.g., "int8_v2_awq")
- layout_tag: e.g., "kv-contiguous", "kv-chan-major", "kv-rowpad-64"
- scale_semantics: "per_channel_affine", "shared_scale", "fp8_e5m2_bias"
- supports_kv_read_compat: "true|false" (does this kernel guarantee bitwise-readability of KV entries generated under previous kernel with same model_version?)
- replacement_policy: "inplace_compatible" | "require_invalidation" | "fallback_allowed"
- alignment_bytes: integer string (e.g., "64")
- requires_cache_rewrite: "true|false"

Per-kernel constraints and recommended enforcement behavior:
1) INT8 (per-channel affine)
- Characteristic: compact, relies on per-channel zero-point and scale vectors. Layout often splits quant params per-row.
- KV concern: raw int8 storage is not directly readable by FP kernels; reading requires dequantization with the same scale/zero-point.
- Descriptor: supports_kv_read_compat must be true only if model packaging includes scale vectors persisted in KV header.
- Enforcement:
  - If kernel_cap_id changes between predictions and both sides have supports_kv_read_compat == true and layout_tag matches, allow in-place read.
  - Otherwise, require KV invalidation prior to switching to a non-compatible kernel or perform an automatic rewrite pass (costly) under scheduler coordination.

2) FP8 (E5M2/E4M3 variants)
- Characteristic: narrower dynamic range than FP16; many implementations store FP8 packed bytes with per-tensor or per-block exponent bias.
- KV concern: FP8 -> FP16/FP32 upcast is lossful but safe for read; FP8 produced under one exponent-bias policy may be unreadable by another.
- Descriptor: scale_semantics should include bias policy; supports_kv_read_compat true only if identical bias policy and layout_tag.
- Enforcement:
  - If bias differs, require rewrite or invalidation.
  - For mixed FP8 families that advertise identical bias and layout, allow transparent transition; emit metric quant.kv.read_compat=true.

3) GPTQ
- Characteristic: compressed weight layout, often uses custom permutation and scaling stored in model artifact. Runtime kernel uses unpack+dequant path.
- KV concern: GPTQ kernels sometimes store intermediate activations in higher-precision scratch and do not reuse the same KV layout; supports_kv_read_compat is commonly false.
- Enforcement:
  - Default: require KV invalidation when switching between GPTQ and any other family.
  - Exception: model-specific packaging can declare a compatibility shim; that must include a fast rewrite routine registered in the kernel registry.

4) AWQ
- Characteristic: row-wise non-uniform quantization with per-row scales, often optimized for matmul with special memory stride.
- KV concern: AWQ-generated KV may be unreadable by standard per-channel INT8 consumers.
- Enforcement:
  - Unless explicit supports_kv_read_compat==true and identical layout_tag, invalidate KV on model swap.
  - If supports_kv_read_compat is true but alignment_bytes differs, the loader must realign the KV (cheap copy) under lock.

KV cache invariants and lifecycle rules:
- Invariant 1: Every KV cache chunk is annotated with a KV header that includes kernel_cap_id and model_version. Runtime checks header before using any entry.
- Invariant 2: Reads are only allowed when kernel_cap_id matches the executing kernel OR when the executing kernel declares read_compat and layout_tag matches.
- Invariant 3: Any write that would change header fields (e.g., model_version bump or kernel_cap_id change) must be serialized with an exclusive lock on that KV chunk.
- Lifecycle transitions:
  - Warm start (same model_version, same kernel_cap_id): no action needed.
  - Sticky kernel upgrade (kernel_cap_id changes but supports_kv_read_compat==true and layout matches): use shared lock during rewrite pass; allow concurrent reads but block writes only briefly. Rewrite can be incremental (per-layer) with metrics emitted per-layer.
  - Incompatible swap: invalidate KV chunk and emit quant.kv.invalidation{model,old_cap,new_cap} metric. Invalidation is a simple header tombstone plus background eviction; running requests detect tombstone and either fallback or fail-fast depending on route policy.

Scheduler locking model (primitives):
- Locks:
  - KV_SHARED(lock_id): lightweight reader lock allowing concurrent readers and single writer per chunk. Optimized for fast reentrant read-paths used by generation.
  - KV_EXCLUSIVE(lock_id): writer lock used during header changes and rewrite. Acquired with priority to in-flight token completions to bound latency impact.
  - MODEL_LOAD_SEMAPHORE(model_id): controls concurrent model kernel swaps to avoid THP/oom spikes; coarse-grained.

- Lock acquisition rules (ordered to avoid deadlock):
  1) MODEL_LOAD_SEMAPHORE (if model swap/upgrade required)
  2) KV_EXCLUSIVE (when performing invalidation or rewrite)
  3) KV_SHARED for normal generation reads
- Practical rule: do not hold MODEL_LOAD_SEMAPHORE while holding KV_SHARED for more than 2ms in the hot path. Use optimistic double-check pattern: grab KV_SHARED, confirm header, read; if header mismatch detected, drop KV_SHARED and escalate to MODEL_LOAD_SEMAPHORE + KV_EXCLUSIVE flow.

Fallback and error semantics:
- Graceful fallback to higher-precision path is possible when:
  - The fallback kernel supports reading the KV format (supports_kv_read_compat true) or when the route policy "fallback_allowed" is set.
  - Otherwise, follow the route policy which can be one of: "invalidate_and_restart", "fail_fast", "enqueue_model_reload".
- When invalidation occurs mid-request (rare), the runtime must:
  1) complete the current token generation if kernel already consumed KV (idempotent), then mark request as needing a retry under the new model; or
  2) if not consumed, immediately translate to fallback path.
- Metrics to emit on all transitions: quant.kv.invalidation.count, quant.kv.rewrite.latency_p50/p95, quant.kv.read_compat.success, quant.kv.read_compat.failure, quant.kernel.swap.duration.

Testing and verification matrix:
- Unit tests per kernel descriptor verifying header checks and read-compat branching.
- Integration tests simulating: (a) model swap during active generation (high QPS case) (b) scheduled kernel upgrade across many batches (c) forced alignment change requiring cheap rewrite.
- Fuzz tests: random sequences of model_version and kernel_cap_id swaps while the KV cache is hot to ensure deterministic invalidation and no memory corruption.
- Performance tests: measure median generation latency with locks in place; goal is <1.05x baseline for shared-lock reads and <1.15x during incremental rewrite.

Operational playbook (short):
- When telemetry shows increased quant.kv.invalidation.count for a specific model_id:
  1) check compatible kernel releases in the last 24h (git tags / model registry).
  2) identify clients with mixed kernel_cap_id in headers; add routing pin for stable kernel where possible.
  3) consider a controlled rewrite (scheduled low-QPS window) using MODEL_LOAD_SEMAPHORE coordination and per-layer incremental rewrite.

Backward compatibility and future extensions:
- We plan to introduce a compact binary capability manifest embedded in model artifacts to speed runtime checks. Future fields: sample_size_hash (to ensure quant scale alignment), per-layer-layout-hash, and a rewrite-hint (estimated cost).
- Long-term: explore on-device microshims that allow lossless on-the-fly translation between compatible quant formats to reduce invalidations.

Appendix: quick compatibility summary (human-readable):
- INT8 <-> INT8 (same layout & scale persisted): compatible (in-place read)
- INT8 <-> FP8: incompatible unless model package provides explicit shim+rewrite
- GPTQ <-> any other: incompatible by default (require invalidation)
- AWQ <-> per-channel INT8: often incompatible; allow read only with declared supports_kv_read_compat and equal alignment

Open questions (for triage):
- Should we persist scale vectors for INT8-produced KV entries by default? Cost / memory tradeoff needs quantification.
- How to version capability descriptors in a way that is compact and backwards compatible across model registry upgrades?
- Can we safely allow cross-node KV reuse when kernel_cap_id differs but read_compat is true? (network-level consistency required)

Action items (owners):
- Arjun: prototype header-check fast-path in the runtime (RINF-1342) by 2025-02-20.
- Lucia: add unit tests for invalidation & rewrite paths in CI by 2025-02-10.
- Maya: schedule perf runs comparing shared lock costs, target 1.05x baseline by 2025-02-28.

Notes: this is a working draft; the intent is to lock down the minimal descriptor and locking primitives quickly so kernel teams and model-packagers can iterate independently. Please add comments inline on the Confluence page linked above and reference RINF-1342 for implementation tracking.
